proof.native_title: What is the effect of alarmist media and radiofrequency electromagnetic field (RF‐EMF) exposure on salivary cortisol and non‐specific symptoms?

candidate_claims.text: Symptoms increased under openly known exposure compared with known non-exposure. The alarmist-video manipulation increased perceived risk but did not significantly change the symptom or cortisol outcomes in the reported factorial comparisons.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 12 to 16, Results and Discussion

candidate_claims.text: Because actual exposure and knowledge were bundled in the open condition, the study cannot isolate a pure RF effect. Cortisol timing, anticipatory stress, limited sensitivity to small effects and the nonclinical sample constrain interpretation.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 15 to 17, Discussion and limitations

proof.native_title: Exposure Perception and Symptom Reporting in Idiopathic Environmental Intolerance Attributed to Electromagnetic Fields Using a Co‐Designed Provocation Test

candidate_claims.text: The study did not demonstrate consistent exposure detection or exposure-related symptoms at the collective level. A nominal individual detection finding did not persist when the least-certain session was removed, so that exception should not be treated as robust detection.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 14 to 16, individual and collective interpretation

candidate_claims.text: Perceived exposure was associated with symptom reporting, but these joint self-reports do not prove a clinical nocebo mechanism. Small selected series, heterogeneous individualized protocols and multiple comparisons limit generalization beyond the tested sessions.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 15 to 17, Discussion and limitations

proof.native_title: Impact of mobile phone-specific electromagnetic fields on DNA damage caused by occupationally relevant exposures: results of ex vivo experiments with peripheral blood mononuclear cells from different demographic groups

candidate_claims.text: The highest tested RF condition increased comet-assay signal in the older normal-weight pooled cells, while lower conditions and younger groups did not show that pattern. The tested combined treatments generally did not enhance chemically induced damage; selected decreases are not evidence of clinical protection.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 5 to 9, Results, combined-treatment tables and Discussion

candidate_claims.text: Pooled cells and sparse independent experiments cannot describe individual donor susceptibility or cancer risk. Differences in demographic composition, culture conditions and technical replicate wording constrain interpretation of this laboratory DNA-damage endpoint.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods; pages 8 to 9, Discussion

proof.native_title: Autonomous nervous system responses to environmental‐level exposure to 5G's first deployed band (3.5 GHz) in healthy human volunteers

candidate_claims.text: Selected regional skin-temperature and electrodermal measures differed across the tested conditions, while not every measure showed an exposure-related finding. These physiological responses do not themselves establish cognitive improvement, injury or disease.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 11, Results, Figures and Discussion

candidate_claims.text: The authors restrict interpretation to the tested short-term conditions and call for confirmation. Small selected samples, related repeated measurements and unresolved direction or labeling questions require restraint; no numerical or uniform-direction electrodermal summary is released.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 10 to 11, Discussion and Conclusion

proof.native_title: 1.7 GHz long-term evolution radiofrequency electromagnetic field with stable power monitoring and efficient thermal control has no effect on the proliferation of various human cell types

candidate_claims.text: With thermal and power control, the measured proliferation and selected cell-cycle, stress or DNA-damage assays did not show a significant RF-related pattern. Disabling cooling changed temperature and growth-related measurements, emphasizing the importance of exposure-system control.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 11, Results, Figures and Discussion

candidate_claims.text: A cooling-disabled comparison changes thermal conditions together with the exposure setup and does not establish a universal explanation for every prior study. Limited independent replication and nonsignificant cellular comparisons are not proof of equivalence, human safety or absence of all tissue-specific effects.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 8 to 11, Discussion and experimental limitations
